reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates L1₀ ordering and a three-order-of-magnitude coercivity increase for FeCoNiMnCu with 50 at.% Pt after RTA, but the hypothesis proposes FeCoNi (without Mn, Cu) as the base alloy, which is not directly tested. The mechanism and RTA conditions are supported, but the specific base composition is a gap.
premises: Adding 50 at.% Pt to FeCoNi-based films and applying RTA induces an L1₀-ordered intermetallic phase
The L1₀ phase enhances coercivity by up to three orders of magnitude relative to undoped FCC films
The coercivity enhancement arises from high magnetocrystalline anisotropy due to lower symmetry and strong spin–orbit coupling from Pt
The proposed RTA conditions (700–800°C, ~15 s) are sufficient to form the L1₀ phase without dewetting or phase separation
The baseline FCC FeCoNi film has coercivity below 100 Oe
